scope: Small sealed two-phase channel sensitivity to number of gas cells across a sharp VOF interface. This diagnostic cannot establish the cause of a pressure/temperature offset in the apparatus.
limits: Base experiment uses laminar turbulence and Pr=1e9 to suppress thermal diffusion; it isolates a two-phase interface/discretization sensitivity under a sealed-gas analytical limit.
All meshes share fixed Euler dt=0.00025 s, physical geometry, forcing and initial inventories; the interface is aligned at x=0.8 m.
Pressure comparisons use the gas-volume-weighted pressure log at actual native gas volume. Native gas mass-weighted T and exact Ug use output fields every 0.05 s.

Native field internal energy is Ug=sum(alpha.air*p*V)/(gamma-1), with cell volumes 1e-4/N from the uniform block mesh. Gas p dV work is trapezoid-integrated from every-step scalar p and gas-volume histories.
The 1-D test is a mechanism sensitivity, not direct proof of the main apparatus pressure offset cause.

changes: Dense time_history_rows are provided once in gas-layer-grid-history.csv, rather than repeated in the summary JSON.

The raw final target_expansion_ratio label contained the measured final ratio; it is retained as actual_expansion_ratio and target_expansion_ratio now records the declared target. No measured pressure, temperature, volume, mass or energy observable was changed.

declared_physical_inputs.geometry: 1.0 m axial rectangular sealed channel, 0.01 m by 0.01 m cross-section; gravity zero; water initially x=0..0.8 m; sealed air x=0.8..1 m; initial water 80 mL and gas 20 mL.

initial_state.water_only_withdrawal: x=0 patch; fixed normal velocity; outlet remains water-covered by target endpoint.

thermodynamics.thermal_limit: Pr=1e9 intentionally suppresses molecular diffusion, matching the prior analytical benchmark.
